text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- If Bosnia's Dayton peace agreement fails it will open a path for new conflicts and complete destabilisation of the Balkans, the country's Moslem chairman of the collective Presidency Alija Izetbegovic said after a meeting with U.S. State Secretary Madeleine Albright.
- Haris Silajdzic, Moslem co-chairman of Bosnian central government arrives in Egypt to meet President Hosni Mobarak.
- Bosnian minister for foreign trade and economy Hasan Muratovic and U.S. president's special envoy to Bosnia Claude Ganz discuss easing of legal procedures for foreign investors in Bosnia.
-The International Committe of the Red Cross (ICRC) launches a new campaign to search for missing people.
- Avaz poll shows that 52 percent of pollees think that Bosnian Moslems cannot preserve the integrity of Bosnia Herzegovina alone.
- Sarajevo is supplied with only 20 percent of gas and on March 27 we expect the gas supply to be reduced to a minimum, a gas company official says.
- Pope John Paul II will lead a Mass for 60,000 people at the biggest soccer stadium in Sarajevo April 13, Roman Catholic clergy says.
- Economic delegation from Malaysia discussed possibilities of investment into Bosnia's steel-work industry in central Bosnia.

- Ejup Ganic, vice-president of Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation thinks that opposing division of Bosnia is the only alternative for the country and says that Serbia and Croatia are no longer powerful enough to divide Bosnia.
- After breaking a chain of smuggling Turkish Kurds to western Europe, Sarajevo canton police says Kurds are now returning voluntarily to Turkey.
- The World Bank is satisfied with dynamics of used funds approved for Bosnia, the banks's executive says in an interview.

- U.N. Special Rapporteur for Human Rights for former Yugoslavia Elisabeth Rehn criticizes investigation and trial against three Croats policemen involved in February 10 Mostar incident during her talks with U.N. Secretary-General Koffi Annan.
- Sarajevo's Franciscans return to their monastery in Sarajevo suburb of Nedzarici after they were expelled by Bosnian Serbs in 1992.
- Bosnian Chamber of Commerce to host a first forum on foreign investment and resconstruction in Sarajevo on Wednesday. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
